extracted.intended_audience: ProPublica newsroom staff, journalists, and the organization's readers/interested public
extracted.subtask_description: Organizational principles and guardrails governing how a news organization (ProPublica) may use AI in reporting, editing, and publication, including responsibilities for verification, transparency, integrity, and data protection. Intended to guide journalists' day-to-day decisions and disclosures to readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Our journalists are responsible for everything we publish. If AI is used in our work, it must be reviewed by staff and meet the same editorial standards as the rest of our journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AI usage does not relieve journalists or editors of responsibility; staff review is required and AI-assisted material must conform to existing editorial policies and fact-checking practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification
rubrics_metrics.description: We treat AI-generated material as unverified source material. Because these tools can produce errors, fabricate information or reflect bias, we independently verify facts and claims before publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not accept AI outputs as factual without independent corroboration; anticipate hallucinations, factual errors, and biased outputs and verify against primary sources or human expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: If AI plays a meaningful role in the reporting of a story, we will clearly disclose its use to our audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be as truthful and transparent about how AI is used as with other operations; disclosures should communicate meaningful influence of AI on reporting, analysis, or content production to readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: We do not use AI to generate or manipulate images, audio or video in ways that could mislead our audience. Moreover, AI tools do not replace the original reporting, analysis and judgment of our journalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibit deceptive multimedia manipulation via AI; maintain that AI is a tool that supplements but does not substitute for human reporting, analysis, editorial judgment, and contextualization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy and security
rubrics_metrics.description: We protect our sources, subjects and data by ensuring sensitive or confidential information is handled only through secure, trusted systems. We take care not to input confidential source documents into public AI tools that could compromise data privacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid uploading confidential or identifying source material to public AI services; use secure systems for sensitive data and follow existing source-protection and data-security practices when using AI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Care, caution, and ongoing assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: At every step of the way, we intend to move forward with care and caution. We will continue to assess the efficacy of AI in our journalism and update our guardrails as the technology and our use of it evolve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt an iterative, conservative approach to AI adoption: monitor outcomes, revise policies and guardrails over time, and be prepared to change practices as risks and capabilities evolve.
